newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks drift down in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks drift down in thin trading.

text.p: Colombian stocks continued their downward drift in thin trade dominated by dealing in the country's leading bank, brokers said Wednesday.
Bogota's IBB general price index dipped 0.19 percent to 852.77 in 504.3 million peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED index slid 0.49 percent to 13,383.23 in 376.9 million peso volume.
"The biggest movers today were difficult-to-sell shares, while there was not much movement in blue chips, with the exception of Banco Ganadero," one Bogota broker said.

Banco Ganadero was the highlight of the day's session on the Bogota exchange, down 0.78 percent to 253 in trade of 169 million pesos. Cement manufacturer Cementos Argos remained unchanged at 5,400 in turnover of 156.4 million pesos.

"Banco Ganadero is the first share that investors looking for extra liquidity put up for sale, but they usually do it in small volumes so as not to get rid of their entire holding. Its price stayed steady for most of the day, but dipped on the back of a sale late in the day," the broker added.
Supermarket chain Cadenalco rose 1.13 percent to 890 in 51 million peso trade, bouncing back from recent losses.

"Cadenalco didn't suffer as badly as expected and recovered slightly from the effects of its third quarter results. Now investors trust the supermarket will fare well in the lead-up to Christmas," another Bogota broker said. Other heavily traded stocks in Bogota were Banco Selfin, unchanged at 200 and chemical manufacturer Proficol, steady at 2,950.

In Medellin, trade was dominated by Cementos Argos, which remained unchanged at 5,400 pesos in a session total of 160 million pesos. Supermarket chain Almacenes Exito was also unchanged at 2,600 on a 67 million peso volume.
